headline: Voted to issue an enforcement order at 461 Northampton Street and ratify one at 98 Lower Westfield Road.
summary: The 5 Appleton Street enforcement order was continued to October 8, 2026, while the owner works on a soil remediation plan. Other items covered tree planting plans, a flood pump station project, and ATV damage to trees on conservation trails.
decisions: Continued the 5 Appleton Street enforcement order to October 8, 2026, 7-0.

Approved Commissioner Normand as the Conservation Commission's CPAC representative, succeeding Vice Chairperson Moriarty, 7-0.
Approved the minutes of the May 28, June 11, and June 25, 2026 meetings, 7-0.

plain_text:
Page 1 of 5 
 
Holyoke Conservation Commission Meeting 
Minutes 9/24/26 
Conservation Commission Members Present: Jeffery Horan (Chairperson), Mary Moriarty (Vice Chairperson), 
Patricia Normand, John Perdrizet, Bernice Bowler, Rosemary Arnold, Michael Dodge 
 
Conservation Commission Members Absent: None 
 
Staff Present: Joseph Pellegrino (Director of Conservation and Sustainability)  
 
Members of the Public Present: Randy Reynolds, Sara Berryman (VHB) 
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Chairperson Horan called the meeting to order at 6:18 p.m.   
 
2. Enforcement Order – Continued from 8/13/26 
Location: 5 Appleton Street (MBP: 049-01-006) 
Description: Grading and fill deposition along approximately 470 lineal feet of banks within Riverfront, Banks, and 
Priority and Estimated Habitats of Rare Species associated with the Connecticut River. Fill sediments and 
associated debris were observed eroding down the steep bank towards the water. 
 
Chairperson Horan greeted Mr. Randy Reynolds and Ms. Sara Berryman (VHB) with whom they had discussed this 
project previously.  Mr. Pellegrino reported that a second silt fence and hay wattles had been installed.  Riprap or 
large stone had been placed along the first silt fence nearest the river, and the wattles had been adjusted to 
overlap.  Photographs of the current site conditions were placed in the Commission’s Google Drive.  Based on the 
site visit, the erosion-control measures generally appeared stable.  He confirmed that Mr. Reynolds and Ms. 
Berryman have submitted a Natural Heritage application which is under review, under a 30-day decision window.  
More information for the application has been requested, which Mr. Reynolds intended to send the following day. 
 
Chairperson Horan asked Mr. Reynolds to provide a summary of the remediation.  Mr. Reynolds reported two 
locations that may be disturbed, and clarified that the plan is more to add on to what is already there.  He 
commented on the asbestos concentration which was below 1% and therefore characterized as non-regulated. Vice 
Chairperson Moriarty informed that MassDEP requirements will call for a soil remediation plan when asbestos at 
all is found near wetlands.  The Commission agreed that the applicable requirements must be confirmed before 
restoration work proceeds.  Mr. Reynolds expressed intentions to get in touch with the nearby railroad to make 
sure they approve of whatever plan is enacted.   
 
The Commission discussed the importance of having a soil remediation plan, and noted that there is some urgency 
due to the end of the growing season being in about four weeks.  Mr. Reynolds hoped to have the answers for the 
next Conservation Commission meeting.  Vice Chairperson Moriarty suggested that later in the evening they could 
up look MassDEP rules on asbestos in soil to get things moving, and Mr. Pellegrino suggested a person they might 
reach out to the Circuit Rider for that information.  Mr. Reynolds voiced his intend to come up with a draft of a plan.  
Chairperson Horan asked Vice Chairperson Moriarty of her opinion of what information they should have in the 
event that a remediation plan is not required, expressing his own thought that they should at least identify which 
areas the asbestos was found in.  Vice Chairperson Moriarty pointed out that they may be able to confirm just from 
GPS data where the asbestos was found.  Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked Ms. Berryman whether they have an LSP
Page 2 of 5 
 
at VHP to inspect soil, and Mr. Berryman answered that she can check to see if there is one in the Massachusetts 
office.   
 
Commissioner Bowler made a motion to continue the matter to the October 8, 2026 meeting, and Commissioner 
Dodge seconded the motion.  The motion carried unanimously, 7-0. 
3. Enforcement Order  
Location: 98 Lower Westfield Road (MBP: 174-00-021)  
Description: Illegal dumping and altering of bordering vegetated wetland within the 200’ buffer of Tannery Brook 
 
The Commission reviewed a complaint concerning illegal concrete dumping and alteration within the buffer to the 
bordering vegetated wetland associated with Tannery Brook.  The property is behind the Starbucks and Popeyes 
near the Holyoke Mall. 
 
Mr. Pellegrino reported that property owner Ned Barowsky had received the certified notice and contacted his 
property manager.  The property manager contacted construction services, which agreed to remove the hardened 
concrete.  He reported he visited the site the previous morning and saw no change to the cement.  The affected area 
was estimated at approximately 3' by 5' near the top of the wetland bank.  Concrete dust remained on nearby 
shrubs, but no runoff or material was observed extending toward the brook. 
 
The Commission discussed whether the enforcement order should name both the contractor and the property 
owner.  Members noted that the property owner may not have directed the dumping, but in the case of a 
remediation plan, they would have to be involved in the process.  Commissioner Normand inquired as to whether 
barriers could be erected to prevent this from happening again, being unfamiliar with the property herself.  Mr. 
Pellegrino shared images of the site, showing where the concrete had been dumped, and Vice Chairperson Moriarty 
confirmed that what Commissioner Normand asked is not possible.  Commissioner Dodge commented on how the 
foliage stopped the construction company from going too far in, placing the material within the 50-foot buffer zone 
of the stream. 
 
The Commission acknowledged and discussed the difficulties of construction companies having to get rid of their 
cement before it hardens. Chairperson Horan noted that this does not excuse the illegal dumping of concrete, and 
that construction companies need to address the issue of what to do with excess concrete every time. Chairperson 
Horan described his own experience as dealing with cement truck drivers expressing to him the urgency of 
working fast so cement would not harden. Commissioners expressed discontent and frustration with the idea that 
the illegal dumping of concrete may be common practice. 
 
Commissioner Bowler suggested ratifying Mr. Pellegrino's enforcement, picking a deadline for removal, and then 
deciding how much of a fine to issue.  Commissioner Dodge explained the importance of involving both the 
construction company and property owner so as to assure that somebody will be held responsible. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to ratify the enforcement order against the construction services and the 
property, and Commissioner Perdrizet seconded the motion.  But Mr. Pellegrino informed that he has to double-
check whether they are both included on the enforcement order that he mailed out to them.  Mr. Pellegrino shared 
an image of his enforcement order via Zoom for the Commission to review.  The Commission deliberated on how to 
properly proceed since the language of the form seems to imply that it's intended to list only one party as Violator.  
The Commission decided that the enforcement order was acceptable as written, and clarified that both the 
involved parties will be asked to attend the next Conservation Commission meeting on October 8th, as stated on the 
form.  The motion passed unanimously, 7-0.
Page 3 of 5 
 
4. Discussion – Friendly Enforcement Order, 461 Northampton Street (MBP: 223-00-011) 
The Commission had received an email from TIM HAMMILL on September 7th reporting equipment use for a 
potential tree removal at 461 Northampton Street.  Mr. Pellegrino had visited the site the following day and 
observed a chipper, mini excavator, cut pine logs, and a substantial pile of wood chips.  Mr. Pellegrino discussed the 
matter with Chairperson Horan and decided a friendly enforcement order was appropriate due to the lighter work.  
Mr. HAMMILL sent another email on the 14th reporting that he could hear large equipment.  Mr. Pellegrino 
conducted another site visit on the 18th, noticing that the mini excavator was gone and the chip pile had gotten 
larger.  He reported that he hasn't gotten a return receipt from certified mail at that property.  He said his next step 
is to make sure they send a normal mailing.  He reported that the home is registered to R&R Home Improvement, 
and that Holyoke GIS traces back to the neighbor at 475 Northampton Street, Nilsa Laboy.  He explained that it 
appeared a pine tree had cut down, and that it can be determined from a provided satellite image where it was. 
 
Mr. Pellegrino shared an image of the letter sent to Nilsa Laboy.  Commissioner Dodge inquired as to why 
specifically a friendly enforcement order was issued given the history Ms. Laboy's noncompliance with the 
Conservation Commission, and Mr. Pellegrino explained his process and how he was initially unaware that Ms. 
Laboy owned R&R Home Improvement.  Chairperson Horan clarified that, had they known from the outset, a 
standard enforcement order with the possibility of fines and remediation would have been issued.  Mr. Pellegrino 
shared a map of the property to clarify the location of the buffer zone and the things in question.  They determined 
that the chip pile and equipment was within the 100-foot buffer zone, but they could not determine conclusively 
whether the removed tree was. 
 
Commissioner Dodge moved to issue an enforcement order to Nilsa Laboy and R&R Home Improvement 
concerning the wood chip pile and equipment within the 100-foot wetland buffer at 461 Northampton Street, with 
the order being mailed to 475 Northampton Street.  Commissioner Perdrizet seconded the motion.  The motion 
carried unanimously, 7-0. 
5. Discussion – Executive Order on Tree Pit Restoration, Stump Removal, and Urban Tree 
Planting 
 
Mr. Pellegrino reported that he, DPW Director Mike Gallagher, Stormwater Coordinator, and Grant Writer Miira 
Gates met with Mayor Garcia on September 14th to present the updated implementation plan.  The Mayor 
supported the plan and asked that pruning and removal decisions be based on documented tree condition and 
public safety needs.  The parties plus Chairperson Horan are to meet on the following day, September 25th, to 
discuss the draft supplemental budget to be submitted to City Council on October 20th.  CAFO TJ Plante is expected 
to join the group the following week to discuss potential available funds.   
 
Chairperson Horan informed of a plan to create a four-person in-house crew to include new City Forester, two tree 
climbers and a maintenance worker.  He noted that new equipment will be needed such as a new chipper.   
 
6. Discussion – Demographic, Health & Environmental Equity Profile – ReGreen Springfield 
Report 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked whether the Demographic Health & Environmental Equity plan is included in the 
plan to respond to the Mayor's executive order.  Chairperson Horan that they aren't at that point yet, and that a 
tree inventory followed by a tree removal plan is next on the agenda.  Mr. Pellegrino shared images of the 
Demographic Health & Environmental Equity report by David Bloniarz which Vice Chairperson Moriarty had been 
referring to, explaining the information it contains and its purpose.  He stated that the report looks at 
environmental justice criteria around the City of Holyoke.  It compares Holyoke neighborhoods based on reported 
needs such as socioeconomic burden, tree canopy coverage, impervious surface, and related environmental justice 
factors, providing a plan for tree planting.  The profile can support grant applications and help prioritize future tree
Page 4 of 5 
 
planting and public education.  It can be used to form a five-year citywide forestry management cycle, and there 
could be funds available for it such as a DCR grant of up to $100,000 for tree planting.  Chairperson Horan 
expressed enthusiasm for the report. 
 
7. Formal Vote – New CPAC Representative 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty had served for five years as the Conservation Commission’s CPAC representative.  She 
nominated and made a motion for Commissioner Normand to succeed her, and Commissioner Normand accepted 
the nomination.  Commissioner Arnold seconded the motion, which passed unanimously, 7-0. 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty reported that the amount of money received this year will be much reduced since the 
City voted to reduce the contribution.  Approximately $550,000 was available for more than $2 million in eligible 
applications, barely a quarter, compared to over $1 million the previous year.   
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty also informed that the Waterfront Tavern had requested CPA funding for stairs and a 
dock in the river, and she had told them that any work at the property would require an NOI to be brought to the 
Conservation Commission.   
 
Commissioner Arnold voiced her desire to bring another idea to the ballot to get CPA funds back to where they 
were previously, hoping that newly-appointed Commissioner Normand can work towards that goal.   
 
8. Formal Vote – Minutes from 5/28/26, 6/11/26, and 6/25/26 Meeting 
 
The Commission reviewed the meeting minutes dated May 28th, June 11th, and June 25th, 2026.  Commissioner 
Bowler reported that only minor grammatical errors were found with no substantial corrections needed.  Vice 
Chairperson Moriarty complimented the transcriptionist's work considering the difficulty in making minutes for 
the Commission's meeting style especially lacking knowledge about environment protection and law.  She 
explained that she spent multiple hours correcting drafts and noted certain omitted details that she thinks ought to 
be added in, and expressed that she probably didn't catch every single one.  She also clarified that the minutes 
Commissioner Bowler had reviewed were Vice Chairperson Moriarty's revised editions.  They look forward to 
hiring Sean to be trained for doing minutes in the future, possibility eliminating the need for a contractor. 
Commissioner Bowler moved to approve the meeting minutes of 5/28, 6/11 and 6/25, and Commissioner Dodge 
seconded the motion, which passed unanimously, 7-0. 
9. Discussion – Upcoming Items for 10/8/26 Meeting 
 
Mr. Pellegrino reported that Tighe & Bond submitted an NOI for the City of Holyoke Engineering Department based 
on item 9 in the Google Drive for work involving seven flood pump stations.  The scope of the project was larger 
than initially understood and may require substantial Commission review.  The first hearing could be done at the 
following October 8th meeting, though with other agenda items Chairperson Horan noted that they wouldn't be 
able to address the project in great detail.  
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty discussed the 5 Appleton Street enforcement order and voiced her discontent with the 
placement of riprap, since Mr. Reynolds was clearly told that no work is to be done at the 8/13 meeting aside from 
what the Commission specifically requested. Chairperson Horan noted that, based on the notes from the site visit, 
that some work to stabilize erosion controls was authorized. Mr. Pellegrino pulled up site photos to confirm the 
presence and extent of the riprap. Commissioners noted that the amount of material brought to the site far exceeds 
the “one or two rocks” that the property owner was requested to place along the erosion controls. Chairperson 
Horan concurred that the amount of riprap brought it was excessive. Vice Chairperson Moriarty pointed out that 
they may have needed soil samples from the area where it was placed, and that the owner of the property may be 
intentionally impeding the soil testing.  The Commission expects to address the matter further at the October 8th 
meeting.
Page 5 of 5 
 
 
Mr. Pellegrino gave an update on the Edna Williams parcel, informing that he took the ANR to the Holyoke Planning 
Board, who then approved it.  He noted that a city councilor questioned the ability to develop the parcel due to not 
having bidders a couple years back after the city went through an RFP.  The planning board chair gave her 
signature on the mylar, and Mr. Pellegrino expected to obtain it and record it at the Registry of Deeds early the 
following week, with a future meeting planned with the City Solicitor and others to get things squared away for 
City Council.   
 
Chairperson Horan reported that he and Commissioner Arnold have noticed increasing ATV use on conservation 
trails near the former Mulcahy properties.  ATV users had damaged or knocked down more than 20 trees, including 
some approximately five inches in diameter, and appeared to extend beyond established trails.  Chairperson Horan, 
Commissioner Arnold and Vice Chairperson Moriarty had followed the trails but were limited by property 
boundaries.  Mr. Pellegrino reported talking to Kevin Chaffee of Massachusetts Fish and Game, who offered to 
participate in a site walk and, if provided reliable coordinates, to bring it up to the EPOs to have them stationed.  
Mr. Pellegrino and the Commission expected to schedule a site walk in the coming week. 
 
10. Adjourn 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty and Chairperson Horan thanked Mr. Pellegrino for his work in preparation for the 
meeting, such as the agenda item review. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 8:29 p.m.
